name: Average-case rigorous algorithms for F_3^n vector subset sum and binary-error LWE (Kothari-Metger-O'Donnell-Shutty-Wu)
description: arXiv 2609.40321 studies vector subset sum over F_3^n (given m random vectors, find a nonempty subset summing to 0) and binary-error LWE over F_q. Via the Chen-Liu-Zhandry Regev-style quantum reduction, a deterministic classical algorithm for binary-error LWE with a proved sample-time tradeoff gives a polynomial-time quantum algorithm with m = eps n^2 vectors for every fixed eps>0; classical F_3-subset-sum is improved to eps=0.1022. Importantly, the technique is algebraic (XL/degree of regularity, Kruskal-Katona, monomial counting), not a collision-counting argument; I found no collision counting in the text. It is the nearest rigorous finite-field analogue of 'subset sum with many relations', average case only.
authors_year_venue: Robin Kothari, Tony Metger, Ryan O'Donnell, Noah Shutty, Kewen Wu; arXiv 2609.40321v1 (quant-ph), 30 Sep 2026; builds on Chen-Liu-Zhandry EUROCRYPT 2022 and Kothari-O'Donnell-Wu STOC 2026.
status_and_verification: Preprint, not peer reviewed. I read the abstract, introduction, table of contents and statements of Theorems 1.3, 1.7 and 1.10 from the full text (alphaXiv extraction); I did not read the proofs in Sections 2-6 and the appendices. A text search for 'collision', 'birthday', 'second moment' in the full extraction returned no matches.
key_theorem_or_bound: Thm 1.3: for any constant kappa>log 3 and every m >= kappa n, a quantum algorithm solves average-case F_3^n-subset-sum with probability 1-2^{-Omega_kappa(m)} in time (m/n)^{O_kappa(ceil(n^2/m))}. Thm 1.7: for q and kappa>log_{q/2}(q), m>=kappa n, a deterministic classical algorithm solves binary-error LWE over F_q in time (m/n)^{O_{q,kappa}(ceil(n^2/m))}. Thm 1.10: for m >= q^{q^2} n^{1+floor((q+3)/4)} a deterministic classical algorithm solves average-case F_q^n-subset-sum in poly(m). Classical F_3: eps = 0.1022 (LLM-assisted optimization per the paper).
regime_exponents: Sample regime m = eps n^2 (polynomial time), m >= kappa n gives quasi-polynomial/exponential interpolation (m/n)^{O(n^2/m)}; at m = Theta(n) time is 2^{O(n log n)}-type, i.e. not below 2^{n/2} meaningfully. These exponents refer to vector length n over F_q, not to the 0.311n / 0.5n / 0.661n thresholds of C1/C2.
proof_type_and_tools: Algebraic/probabilistic: reduction of binary-error LWE to degree of regularity of a polynomial system (Section 2), 'popular pair of variables' argument, Kruskal-Katona shadow bounds for multiset shadow, symbolic rank / martingale step for a probabilistic surjectivity condition, quotient decoding (Sec 4); for subset sums, affine reducible vectors and a recursive algorithm (Sec 5); worst-case F_q^n via a zero-sum identity over rooted trees (Sec 6).
quantitative_loss: Quantum/classical time is (m/n)^{O(ceil(n^2/m))}: super-polynomial unless m = Omega(n^2); success probability 1-2^{-Omega(m)}. Constants depend on q and kappa (e.g. q^{q^2} in Thm 1.10), so the bounds are not exponent-sharp; polynomial-vs-exponential tradeoff is explicit and does not blow up with energy because there is no energy notion.
worst_case_vs_average_case: Average-case over uniform random vectors (Thm 1.3, 1.7 for random LWE samples, 1.10 average-case). Section 6 contains a classical worst-case F_q^n-subset-sum result (Thm 1.11 improves the n-exponent of [KOW26] to q-1) but it is a different regime (many vectors, polynomial in n); no transfer to worst-case {0,1} integer subset sum.
coefficient_set: Coefficients {0,1} over F_q (F_3 mainly), i.e. subset sums in a finite field, not over Z; binary-error LWE has errors in {0,1}.
subset_size_regime: All nonempty subsets; no cardinality restriction. Solutions found have unrestricted size; Theta(n)-subset regime not addressed.
relevance_to_Nc: Weak/indirect. The paper does not bound a number of equal-sum pairs; its tools control the dimension of a quotient of the polynomial ring (degree of regularity). A possible 'template' lesson: replace a collision/energy count by a rank/Hilbert-function count of monomials (Kruskal-Katona shadows). Over Z with {0,1} coefficients the analogous object would be the number of low-weight relations among a_i, which is what N_c counts; whether that can be phrased as a monomial/rank statement is open. Contrary to the task description, the paper is not a collision-counting argument.
relevance_to_Dstar: None directly. D* concerns distinct balanced half-sums over Z; the paper has no analogue. Could only inform a finite-field model of C2 (subset sums in F_3^n with few distinct half-sums).
applicability_gap: Finite field with characteristic 3 vs integers; random inputs vs adversarial; polynomially many vectors m ~ n^2 relative to dimension n (not density-1 subset sum where n numbers live in one dimension); algebraic degree-of-regularity (XL/Grobner) methods rely on the non-existence of low-degree coincidences, not on additive energy; no analogue of Theta(n)-subsets or polynomial doubling.
counterexample_or_hard_instance_family: The paper notes small-m regimes where the problem is conjectured exponentially hard classically (m below eps n^2 with eps<0.1022 for the classical algorithm, possible exponential quantum speedup), but gives no explicit hard instance family. Appendix A concerns satisfiability of the average-case problem and Appendix C degree-3 XL experiments [uncertain] (titles only, contents not read).
dependency_chain: Chen-Liu-Zhandry (Regev quantum reduction) -> Kothari-O'Donnell-Wu STOC 2026 (classical, m~n^2/3) -> this paper (deterministic binary-error LWE with proven sample-time tradeoff, eps=0.1022 classical). Could be composed with BSG/PFR (F_2^n analogues) in a finite-field model of the branch-or-bin argument; not composed in the source.
constructiveness: Fully algorithmic: deterministic classical binary-error LWE decoder (Sec 4.2) and quantum subset sum algorithm via Regev reduction; classical F_q^n subset sum recursive algorithm (Sec 5).
lean_formalizable: Not in a mathlib-free setting for the algebraic parts; the Kruskal-Katona/multiset shadow counting lemma is combinatorial and could be formalized with effort. [uncertain] not checked against the actual proof.
computational_check: Source includes degree-3 XL experiments in Appendix C (scale not read). Repo scripts at n<=40 cannot reproduce F_3^n regimes without new code; a tiny F_3 version (n<=8, m<=n^2/3) is checkable by brute force.
next_experiment: Build a finite-field toy model: random m vectors in F_3^n, count disjoint equal-sum pairs of Theta(m)-subsets and compare to the expectation 3^{-n} * (number of pairs); check whether the variance/second-moment style lower bound on N_c holds for m = c n, as a model for C1's average-case behavior.
open_issues: Optimality of eps=0.1022 is unknown; the classical-quantum gap for m<0.1022 n^2 is open; constants q^{q^2} are loose. The outline's description (collision-counting template) is not supported by the paper text as retrieved; I read only statements, not proofs, so I cannot rule out collision-like lemmas in Sec 5-6. [uncertain] Sec 5-6 details not read.
